territorial_scope.description: Applies nationwide to physicians and medical institutions in Brazil, requiring AI systems to meet norms in force in the national territory.

evidence.quote: utilizar apenas sistemas de IA que atendam às normas éticas, técnicas, legais e regulatórias vigentes no território nacional

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: CFM Resolution 2,454/2026 sets rules for research, development, governance, audit, monitoring and responsible use of AI in medicine. It applies to physicians and medical institutions, requires physician oversight, patient information, risk categorisation (low, medium, high) and governance measures, and takes effect 180 days after publication.
summary.long: Resolution CFM No. 2,454 of 11 February 2026 sets norms for research, development, governance, auditing, monitoring, training and responsible use of AI systems and models in medicine. Its addressees are physicians and medical institutions. They must keep final clinical authority with the physician (Arts. 4, 7, 18-19), inform patients when AI is used as relevant support (Art. 5 §1; Art. 11), protect health data and avoid AI tools without adequate information security (Art. 6), and respect fundamental rights and bioethics across the AI lifecycle (Art. 9). Institutions must perform a preliminary risk assessment (Art. 12) and classify AI solutions as low, medium, high or unacceptable risk under Annex II, informing users of the classification (Art. 13). Annex III lists governance measures, including bias monitoring and mitigation, an algorithmic impact assessment and a Technical Director responsible for oversight. Institutions with in-house systems must create an AI and Telemedicine Committee (Art. 14). Supervision is by the regional medical councils (Art. 15). Violations lead to ethical sanctions, without prejudice to civil and criminal liability (Art. 8). The rules also cover systems in use at entry into force (Art. 21) and the resolution takes effect 180 days after publication (Art. 23).

relations.target_text: Lei nº 3.268, de 30 de setembro de 1957 (regulamentada pelo Decreto nº 44.045, de 19 de julho de 1958)
relations.note: The preamble cites this law as the source of the Council's powers. The text describes Decreto nº 44.045 as regulating that law; the decree is not coded as a separate relation of this resolution.

evidence.quote: no uso das atribuições conferidas pela Lei nº 3.268, de 30 de setembro de 1957, regulamentada pelo Decreto nº 44.045, de 19 de julho de 1958

relations.target_text: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD)
relations.note: Art. 16 requires data used to develop, train, validate and implement AI in medicine to be processed in observance of the LGPD, together with sector information-security rules.

evidence.quote: observando rigorosamente a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD)

relations.note: Art. 7 §1 states that using AI does not exempt the physician from compliance with the Code of Medical Ethics and other CFM norms.

evidence.quote: não exime o médico do cumprimento do Código de Ética Médica

notes: The fetched copy is the DOU web page; its footer says it does not replace the certified version. Art. 13 lists risk levels as baixo, médio, alto or inaceitável, but Anexo II defines only three levels (baixo, médio, alto). Anexo III, item II refers to discontinuation under 'art. 10, §2º', but Art. 10 has no paragraphs and no discontinuation provision. Art. 19 contains a garbled phrase ('consiste no implica seu direito'), and Art. 10 contains a garbled phrase ('sistemas de modelos, sistemas e aplicações de IA da medicina'). Art. 23 sets entry into force 180 days after publication; the publication date (27/02/2026) appears only in the page metadata, not in the operative text. Anexos I to III form part of the resolution.

evidence.provision: Cabeçalho (metadados do DOU, Edição 39, Seção 1, Página 158)

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment. The only number is the 180-day period before entry into force in Art. 23, a procedural time limit (event, not threshold). Risk levels in Art. 13 and Anexo II are qualitative categories, not numeric thresholds.
